name: Oregon

agency.name: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife

overview: Oregon's controlled hunts for deer, elk, pronghorn and spring bear use preference points: 75% of each hunt's tags go to first-choice applicants with the most points and 25% are drawn at random among all other first-choice applicants, so everyone has some chance. Bighorn sheep, Rocky Mountain goat and Premium hunts are pure random draws with no points. Applications (up to five choices per series, $10 per series) are due May 15 (Feb. 10 for spring bear), with results by June 12 (Feb. 20 for spring bear). Nonresidents can receive at most 5% of tags in deer, elk and bear hunts, 3% in pronghorn hunts and 5-10% of sheep and goat tags; starting in 2026, Eastern Oregon deer hunts are organized by Deer Hunt Areas instead of WMUs.

species.drawSystemSummary: Preference-point draw: for each hunt, 75% of tags go to first-choice applicants with the most preference points; the other 25% are drawn at random among all remaining first-choice applicants. Leftover tags then go to 2nd-5th choices at random (points do not count). Applicants who do not draw their first choice, or buy a Point Saver, gain one point for the series. Controlled elk is the 200 series.
species.residentNote: Residents hold at least 95% of tags in each controlled elk hunt. Drawing a first choice resets points to zero (Pioneer and 65+ resident disabled veteran licensees reset to one).
species.nonresidentNote: A maximum of 5% of tags in controlled deer, elk and bear hunts can go to nonresidents; nonresidents get no preference other than their points. Guides and Outfitters Program tags (equal to half the nonresident tags drawn the previous year) reduce nonresident tags available in the draw. Nonresidents may apply for Premium hunts with equal odds.
species.otcSummary: General-season elk tags are sold over the counter: general archery (Aug. 29 - Sept. 27, 2026), West Cascade (Nov. 7-13), Coast 1st (Nov. 14-17) and 2nd (Nov. 21-27) seasons, and the Eastern Oregon Rocky Mountain 2nd season (spike only, listed units, Nov. 7-15). A General Season Antlerless Elk Damage tag is also sold. Premium elk (M series) is a separate random draw for one extra tag per unit. For 2027 (adopted Sept. 18, 2026): the any-legal-weapon coast elk spike-only bag limit moves from the second to the first period, and antlerless elk are removed from the General Archery Season Tag bag limit in the West Cascades hunt.

White-tailed-deer-only controlled hunts: hunts ODFW names 'Whitetail' plus hunts whose regulations bag limit is white-tailed deer only (e.g. 151M Baker Muzzleloader, 152M Grande Ronde Muzzleloader, 157A Lower Wallowa Valley, 649B, 657A Flora, 660A Upper Wallowa Valley; 10 hunts in 2022-2023, 11 in 2024-2025, 29 in 2026 after the switch to Eastern Oregon Deer Hunt Areas). 2025 hunts are classified from the 2024 regulations when the 2025 report lists the same code and name, because the 2025 booklet was not retrieved.
400 series controlled pronghorn plus Premium pronghorn N series (first-choice applicants only). 2026 hunt 470C prints 0 nonresident applicants with 1 nonresident drawn; that count is left blank.
700 series controlled spring bear only (fall bear is general season).

500 series. ODFW publishes only first-choice applicant totals (no drawn counts).
